title: Heat today and the next three days
name: Estimated heat stress (WBGT)
what: Wet-bulb globe temperature (WBGT) is the heat-stress index used in international and national standards for heat at work.
how: The figure here is our estimate for the city as a whole, calculated from forecast air temperature and humidity with the Australian Bureau of Meteorology's simplified formula. That formula assumes fairly strong sun and light wind, and leaves out changes in sun and wind. In cloudy or windy weather, and at night or early in the morning, it is likely to read higher than a measured value.
not: It is not a measurement and not an official warning.
noLevel: No heat-stress level is shown beside the estimate: published WBGT levels are for measured values.
fuller: Researchers comparing methods recommend a fuller calculation for outdoor work, which also uses sun and wind; this page does not use it yet.

method.label: Australian Bureau of Meteorology: Thermal comfort observations, about the approximation to the WBGT

review.label: Lemke and Kjellstrom, 2012: Calculating workplace WBGT from meteorological data, Industrial Health
